title: Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this brake caliper hardware application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by calip bleed port taper-seal screw and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for brake caliper hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g for net-shape tolerance
Go/No-Go ring gauging for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for calip bleed port application
commonFailures: Thread galling Ti-on-Ti assembly - prevented by MoS2 anti-seize compound and -20% installation torque — critical for calip bleed port performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw suitable for Calip bleed port taper-seal screw?
faq.a: Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address brake caliper hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for calip bleed port requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. calip bleed port components require Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for calip bleed port application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Brake Bleed Port Screw includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet calip bleed port specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.
